name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,533

entries.clue: Deny being in favour of proposal (6)

blocks.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
a bid is an offer or proposal

annotation.surface: Someone refuses to admit they backed a proposal.
annotation.walkthrough: "Deny" reads as disowning your support, but here it means refuse permission.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of refusing permission: a parent can deny or forbid a child sweets.

entries.clue: Duck with permit to be a small bird (5)

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
W is the standard abbreviation for with
to let is to permit

annotation.surface: A duck gets a licence to pass as a small bird.
annotation.walkthrough: "Duck" looks like the bird the clue is about, but it is the cricket zero.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a young owl is small, and a bird.

entries.clue: Club that chap joined to go swimming (5)

blocks.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
he is that chap

annotation.surface: A man signs up with a swimming club.
annotation.walkthrough: "Club" suggests a society he joins; it is the thing you hit a ball with.
annotation.definitionFit: To bathe, in British use, is to go for a swim.

entries.clue: It's a problem to raise hat to a girl (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
any girl's name will do; here Emma

annotation.surface: Whether to raise one's hat to a lady is a question of etiquette.
annotation.walkthrough: Raising your hat is a courtesy in the surface; in a down clue it means flip LID upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a choice between two bad options is a kind of problem, and the word is used loosely for any predicament.

entries.clue: Falsehoods which vegetarians would find difficult to swallow (4,4)

definitions.text: which vegetarians would find difficult to swallow

blocks.note: a Cockney rhyming-slang phrase whose second word rhymes with lies

blocks.clueFragment: which vegetarians would find difficult to swallow
blocks.note: a pork pie is a pastry filled with pork, no food for a vegetarian

annotation.surface: Some lies are too much for a vegetarian to believe.
annotation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, pork pies (often cut to porkies) means lies. "Difficult to swallow" is both hard to believe and hard to eat.
annotation.definitionFit: Pork pies rhymes with lies, so in British slang pork pies are falsehoods.

entries.clue: 'Thespian' is term that describes Victoria Wood, perhaps. (7)

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so these words surround the answer

blocks.note: the last four letters of Thespian, all of is, and the first letter of term

annotation.surface: A definition-style note on calling the comedian Victoria Wood a thespian.
annotation.walkthrough: The quote marks invite you to think about the word "Thespian"; its letters are what matter. Victoria Wood was a British comedian and actress who sang her own songs at the piano.
annotation.definitionFit: Victoria Wood played the piano in her comic songs, so she is an example of a pianist.

entries.clue: Crash into back of car - organ death follows (4,3)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
what follows comes after, so organ and death are written after the R

blocks.note: last letter of car
the ear is an organ of hearing
death is the end

annotation.surface: Someone drives into another car's back and a fatal organ failure follows.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crash into back of car" reads as the whole definition, but only "Crash into" is; "back of car" is wordplay, and "follows" orders the pieces after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A motoring idiom: the verb comes from hitting the back of the car in front.

entries.clue: Postman with fancy car - he's on his rounds (9)

blocks.note: Postman Pat, the children's TV character
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

annotation.surface: A postman does his delivery round in a smart car.
annotation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman. A Roller is a Rolls-Royce.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a patrol is a regular circuit, so whoever walks it is on his rounds.

entries.clue: Perhaps the Irish Sea, pure with no variation (9)

indicators.note: a variation of letters is a changed arrangement of them

blocks.note: used as written
used as written
used as written

annotation.surface: The Irish Sea is described as clean and unchanging.
annotation.walkthrough: "The Irish Sea" reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at "the Irish"; "Sea" joins the letters to rearrange, and "no variation" hides an anagram of NO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by "Perhaps": Ireland is in Europe, so its people are one instance.

entries.clue: Pack captures many a naval unit (8)

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

blocks.note: to pack a space is to fill it
a lot is many
used as written

annotation.surface: A wolf pack captures a whole naval unit.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pack" reads as a group of wolves or U-boats; it is the verb, to fill.
annotation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships, a naval unit.

entries.clue: Sweet wine lost in minor quake? (6)

indicators.note: the wine goes missing from inside the quake

blocks.note: an aftershock is a small tremor after an earthquake
hock is German white wine

annotation.surface: A bottle of sweet wine gets broken in a small tremor.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sweet wine" reads as one thing; "Sweet" is the definition and hock is the wine. Afters is British slang for dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: Afters is the British word for the sweet course after the main meal.

entries.clue: Junk mail re-sent to cut out waste (10)

indicators.note: to junk something is to wreck it, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Junk mail keeps being sent again, and someone wants to stop the waste.
annotation.walkthrough: "Junk mail" is a set phrase, but "Junk" is the instruction and only "mail re-sent" is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: To streamline a process is to make it more efficient by cutting out waste.

entries.clue: Ghost briefly makes a comeback; sorry about that (4)

indicators.note: cut short: the last letter goes
comes back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a spook is a ghost

annotation.surface: A ghost returns and apologises for the fright.
annotation.walkthrough: SPOOK loses its last letter to give SPOO, then reads backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Oops is what you say when apologising for a small blunder.

entries.clue: Elderly relative housed in apartment that's gross (8)

indicators.note: the relative is placed inside the apartment

blocks.note: a flat is an apartment
gran is grandmother

annotation.surface: Grandma lives in a dirty flat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Gross" suggests a filthy flat; it means blatant.
annotation.definitionFit: A gross error is a flagrant one: glaring and obvious.

entries.clue: Dilapidated ancestral house of Henry V (9)

indicators.note: run-down and falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A king's crumbling ancestral home.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ancestral house" is a stately home; "house" here is a royal dynasty. Henry V belonged to the House of Lancaster.
annotation.definitionFit: Henry V was a Lancastrian king, of the royal House of Lancaster.

entries.clue: Exotic green clothing for supermarket girl (9)

indicators.note: strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged
the anagram wraps round the supermarket as clothes wrap a body

blocks.note: GREEN rearranged
Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

annotation.surface: A checkout girl wears an unusual green uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: "Supermarket girl" reads as a shop assistant; the supermarket is ALDI and "girl" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: crosswords treat any female first name as "girl".

entries.clue: Cash grab - not 100, but 500 (6)

indicators.note: "not 100" says the grab must lose its hundred, the numeral C
"but 500" supplies what you have instead, so D fills the gap C left

blocks.note: to collar someone is to grab them
C is the Roman numeral for 100
D is the Roman numeral for 500

annotation.surface: A robber grabs cash, taking five hundred rather than a hundred.
annotation.walkthrough: The numbers look like sums of money; they are Roman numerals C and D, and D replaces C in COLLAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the US currency unit is one form of cash, and dollars is also slang for money generally.

entries.clue: Accustomed to setback in older universities (6)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these words
set back, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: ol(DER UNI)versities

annotation.surface: Older universities are used to suffering setbacks.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across the join of "older" and "universities".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of something unpleasant: someone hardened by long exposure is used to it.

entries.clue: Where papers may be posted - possibly about a thousand? (7)

definitions.note: "Where papers may be" is a place, standing for the noun DESKTOP.

indicators.note: the letters of posted might be arranged another way
the anagram goes round the thousand

blocks.note: POSTED rearranged
K, from kilo, stands for a thousand

annotation.surface: Somewhere perhaps a thousand documents have been put up for display.
annotation.walkthrough: "Posted" reads as the end of the definition; it is the anagram fodder. Papers may lie on a desktop, or sit as files on a computer desktop.
annotation.definitionFit: A desktop, the top of a desk or a computer screen, is where papers may be.

entries.clue: VIPs to lead artists' society (3,5)

blocks.note: used as written
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
S is an abbreviation for society

annotation.surface: Important people are chosen to head an artists' society.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lead" reads as the verb, to head; it is the metal, Pb. An RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
annotation.definitionFit: Top brass are the most senior, important people.

entries.clue: It's not exciting messing around outside (7)

indicators.note: messing around with something means fiddling with it carelessly, so its letters end up out of order

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone complains that fooling about outdoors is dull.
annotation.walkthrough: "Outside" looks like a container instruction; it is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym put negatively: something wearisome and dull is the opposite of exciting.

entries.clue: Rings round newspaper proprietors at first for correspondents (3,4)

indicators.note: the proprietors appear only as they are at first, their opening letters N and P
the rings are placed round those two letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
first letters of newspaper proprietors

annotation.surface: Bells ring out around press barons first, for the reporters.
annotation.walkthrough: "Correspondents" suggests newspaper reporters; here it means letter-writers.
annotation.definitionFit: Pen pals are people who write letters to each other: correspondents.

entries.clue: Bird one tells stories about (4)

indicators.note: turned about, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: telling stories is lying

annotation.surface: A bird that someone is spinning yarns about.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tells stories" sounds like a storyteller; to tell stories is also to tell lies.
annotation.definitionFit: The rail is a family of wading birds, including the water rail.

entries.clue: Wild dances and musical in which you may get carried away? (5,5)

definitions.text: in which you may get carried away?

indicators.note: the letters of dances go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: DANCES rearranged
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

annotation.surface: Wild dancing in a musical sweeps the audience off its feet.
annotation.walkthrough: Being carried away usually means swept up by excitement; in a sedan chair you are literally carried by two bearers.
annotation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, so you are carried away in it.

entries.clue: Fence - sit on it? (5)

blocks.note: a boundary round a field, which can be built or grown
"it" is the fence: sitting on the fence means refusing to commit to either side

annotation.surface: A fence, and an invitation to sit on it.
annotation.walkthrough: "It" is the fence of the first definition: to sit on the fence is to hedge.
annotation.definitionFit: A hedge is a living fence, and to hedge is to sit on the fence, avoiding a firm position.

entries.clue: Reason home's on fire in Paris? (5)

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
from the French enfer, hell, the place always on fire

annotation.surface: Someone asks why a house in Paris is burning.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is loose: the French enfer (hell) ends FER, and "in Paris" points to French. "Reason" is the verb, to work something out.
annotation.definitionFit: To infer is to reason your way to a conclusion.

entries.clue: Disciplinarian leaders of schools teach religious instruction classes, typically (6)

indicators.note: the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.clueFragment: schools teach religious instruction classes, typically
blocks.note: first letters of schools, teach, religious, instruction, classes, typically

annotation.surface: Head teachers who enforce discipline also teach RE classes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Leaders of schools" reads as head teachers; it only asks for initial letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Disciplinarian, as an adjective, means strict about rules.

entries.clue: Occasionally he pulled out before day of festival opening (2,3,3)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Onan, in Genesis 38, withdrew rather than father a child
D is the abbreviation for day
used as written
first letter of festival

annotation.surface: A performer withdrew just before the festival's opening day.
annotation.walkthrough: "He pulled out" reads as someone cancelling; it is Onan, the Bible figure known for withdrawal.
annotation.definitionFit: On and off means from time to time: occasionally.

entries.clue: Anticipates Forster (initially) to be included in homework, and Eliot similarly (3-5)

indicators.note: Forster is to be given initially, that is by his initials E. M., not his surname
to be included in something is to be put inside it, so EM goes inside the homework
Eliot is treated the same way as Forster, reduced to his initials T. S.

blocks.note: prep is school homework, from preparation
the novelist E. M. Forster's initials
the poet T. S. Eliot's initials

annotation.surface: A student reads ahead: Forster and Eliot turn up in the homework before the class.
annotation.walkthrough: "Initially" usually means one first letter, but here it means both of Forster's initials, EM. Prep is British school slang for homework.
annotation.definitionFit: To pre-empt something is to act in anticipation of it.

entries.clue: Curses introduction of spectator sports (6)

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is where it starts, its first letter S

blocks.note: first letter of spectator
to sport a hat is to wear it

annotation.surface: Cursing marks a spectator's first taste of sport.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sports" reads as games; it is the verb, to wear showily.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for using bad language, both as verbs in the third person.
